summary: Mirror CPU offload regions across nodes so secondary KV offload tiers work with tensor parallelism across nodes
compatibility: Multi-node tiering with secondary tiers needs the multiprocessing executor with nnodes > 1 and VLLM_HOST_IP set to a specified IP address on every worker, and opens a TCP port on group rank 0 (a free port unless kv_connector_extra_config sets mirror_port) that admits only the remote workers' addresses. Multi-node secondary tiers keyed through FileMapper (fs, obj, p2p) whose rows are not topology-agnostic start from an empty storage namespace; files of the previous one are no longer read or removed. After a cache reset, an OffloadingConnector whose manager promotes from secondary tiers skips lookups (requests recompute) until the flushed jobs report. With secondary tiers, TieringOffloadingSpec releases its /dev/shm region names once mapped and rejects re-registering KV caches, and, when workers may span nodes (nnodes > 1 or Ray), runs node-placement collectives over every data parallel replica at creation; elastic data parallel scaling is not supported and external_launcher is rejected across nodes. Without secondary tiers, regions stay node-local as before. Multi-node tiering with secondary tiers rejects canonical_layout. A multi-worker tiering engine with secondary tiers whose engine core does not share a node with group rank 0 now fails at startup instead of losing remote slots. A mirror copy that fails after its retries is reported as a failed transfer (vllm-1043) instead of stopping the engine.
details: Workers on other nodes mirror their CPU region slots onto the engine-core node, which runs the secondary tiers; the mirror listener admits only the remote workers' addresses.
With secondary tiers, a cache reset skips lookups until every worker reported the jobs it flushed.
With secondary tiers, shared CPU region files are unlinked once mapped, so an engine killed after startup leaves none behind.
